title: The Cure for the Vibe Coding Hangover — Corey J. Gallon, Rexmore
talk_summary: Corey Gallon presents a structured framework for building production software with AI coding agents: 10 principles (spec over prompts, define done first, feature atomicity, dependency-driven sequencing, context engineering) plus a 5-step planning phase and a tight multi-sensory implementation loop. The core mechanism is decomposing work into atomic, fully-specified, dependency-ordered features with executable acceptance criteria and rich feedback (tests + logs + UI/interaction sensors) so agents can self-validate and self-correct autonomously.

takeaways.technique: Atomic feature specs with binary acceptance criteria as the work unit
takeaways.what_they_do: Every feature is decomposed until irreducible, specified with user story + 3-level technical contract + 3-level validation contract, and only then handed to an agent; a feature is 'done' only when tests pass and sensors are clean.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Keep features as small as possible to make agent implementation as successful as possible. We say reduce until irreducible.

takeaways.what_they_do: Synthesize per-feature dependency declarations into a matrix, render a graph, eliminate cycles, then topologically sort into phases where each phase depends only on prior phases; phase gates define when dependent work may start.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Features with no dependencies become phase one. Features depending only on phase one become phase 2.

takeaways.technique: Curated context package via declarative cross-references
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of dumping whole planning docs into the agent, assemble a per-feature context package: the feature spec, only the referenced dependency specs+code, relevant plan sections, and tool-usage guides referenced once and reused.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you're dumping entire planning documents into agent sessions, which wastes context window on irrelevant information

takeaways.technique: Multi-sensory feedback loop (tests + logs + UI/interaction sensors)
takeaways.what_they_do: Agent writes code, immediately executes it, gathers visual (screenshots/state), auditory (logs/errors/stack traces), and tactile (end-to-end interaction) signals, correlates them with test results, and loops until all pass and sensors are clean.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Tests pass, for example, but the UI doesn't render correctly or the workflow completes but errors fill the logs.

takeaways.technique: Binary validation gates per phase instead of percentage tracking
takeaways.what_they_do: Define binary success criteria per phase (which tests must pass, which integration points must work) and track progress as implemented/not-implemented, with no partial credit.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Is a feature implemented or is it not? There is no 20% implementation tracking.

takeaways.technique: Disposable execution sandbox for agent code
takeaways.what_they_do: All agent-written code runs and tests in an isolated, resettable sandbox so agents can experiment and break things with no consequences.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the sandbox provides complete development capabilities in a disposable, risk-free environment with easy reset and no consequences for failure
